patterns.rationale: Matches `get_env` even when U+206A–206F (deprecated format chars) or U+1D173–1D17A (Musical Symbol chars) are interleaved between characters. The two character-class ranges are the exact sets identified in the evasion notes for all three misses. The pattern is narrow: it requires the exact `g-e-t-_-e-n-v` sequence with only these specific invisible chars permitted as separators — no other characters can appear between the letters. NOTE: must be used in a non-raw Python string (or embed the actual Unicode chars) so that `\u` and `\U` are resolved at the string level before `re.compile` sees them.
patterns.fp_notes: The invisible chars (U+206A–206F, U+1D173–1D17A) almost never appear in legitimate prose. The only theoretical FP would be music-notation documentation that happened to place these chars adjacent to the letters g-e-t — vanishingly rare, and not present in any known-good file.

patterns.rationale: Same technique as Pattern 1 but for `send_http`, the exfil relay primitive. Miss 2 encodes `s𝅳e𝅴n𝅵d𝅶_𝅷h𝅸t𝅹t𝅺p` with U+1D173–1D17A; Miss 5 encodes `s⁪e⁫n⁬d⁭_⁮h⁯t⁪t⁫p` with U+206A–206F. Both match this pattern. Same non-raw-string implementation note applies.
patterns.fp_notes: The word "send" with these particular invisible chars between its letters has no legitimate occurrence. Broader `s.*e.*n.*d` would be dangerous but the char-class restriction makes this safe.
